title: Kayseri (ASR) vs Nevşehir (NAV) Airport for Cappadocia
seoTitle: Kayseri (ASR) vs Nevşehir (NAV) Airport for Cappadocia
metaDescription: Nevşehir Kapadokya Airport (NAV) is closer to Göreme (40 km, 35–45 minutes) and Uçhisar (37 km, 35 minutes), while Kayseri Erkilet Airport (ASR) sits…
quickAnswer: [Nevşehir Kapadokya Airport (NAV)](https://epicturkeytravel.com/nevsehir-airport-to-cappadocia/) is closer to Göreme (40 km, 35–45 minutes) and Uçhisar (37 km, 35 minutes), while [Kayseri Erkilet Airport (ASR)](https://cappadocia.taxi/en/blog/which-airport-is-best-for-cappadocia-nevsehir-or-kayseri) sits 70–80 km away (60–75 minutes) but offers far more daily Istanbul flights plus nonstop routes from Antalya and İzmir.

body.text: Which airport is closer to Göreme and Uçhisar?

Nevşehir Kapadokya Airport (NAV) is roughly 30 to 45 kilometers closer to central Cappadocia than Kayseri Erkilet Airport (ASR), cutting 25 to 35 minutes off your ground transfer to Göreme and Uçhisar. Because NAV is a small single-terminal airport, baggage claim and curb exit usually take under 15 minutes.
Distance alone does not tell the whole story if you are staying in Ürgüp or Mustafapaşa on the eastern side of the region, where the drive-time gap shrinks to about 20 minutes.

Drive distances and timings cross-checked against [Paphlagonia Tour](https://paphlagonia-tour.com/blogs/cappadocia-airport-kayseri-or-nevsehir) and [Epic Turkey Travel](https://epicturkeytravel.com/cappadocia-airport-transfer/).
Which has more daily flights from Istanbul?

Kayseri (ASR) has significantly more daily nonstop flights from both Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), operated by Turkish Airlines, [Pegasus Airlines](https://www.flypgs.com/en/cities/flights-to-kayseri), and AJet. Nevşehir (NAV) relies primarily on around three daily [Turkish Airlines](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en/flights-from-istanbul-to-nevsehir) flights from IST plus [AJet](https://ajet.com/en/flights-from-istanbul-to-nevsehir) departures from SAW.

That frequency difference matters when weather or air-traffic delays hit. If a late-afternoon flight to NAV cancels, the next seat may not depart until the following morning—potentially costing you your sunrise balloon window. Flying into ASR gives you multiple same-day rebooking options and typically lower advance fares, especially on early morning or late evening departures.
How much is a private transfer vs shared shuttle?

In 2026, a pre-booked shared shuttle from either NAV or ASR to Göreme, Uçhisar, Avanos, or Ürgüp costs roughly €10 to €15 per person, while a private Mercedes Vito or Sprinter transfer runs €60 to €95 per vehicle depending on airport and group size ([Epic Turkey Travel](https://epicturkeytravel.com/cappadocia-airport-transfer/), [TravelSkyway](https://www.travelskyway.com/en/blog/kayseri-vs-nevsehir-airport-cappadocia-2026)).
There is no direct public city bus from either airport to Göreme or Uçhisar, so you must pre-arrange transport before landing. Choose based on arrival time and party size:

items: Shared shuttle (€10–€15/person): Best for solo travelers or couples landing on daytime domestic flights. Expect a 20–30 minute wait at the terminal while the driver collects passengers from the same flight, plus 2–4 hotel drop-offs along the loop.
Private transfer (€60–€95/vehicle): Better value for families or groups of three or more, and worth the extra €40–€50 for couples arriving after 21:00 who want to sleep before a 04:30 balloon pickup.
Metered airport taxi: Available outside both terminals, though pre-booked fixed-rate private vans usually cost less and guarantee English-speaking dispatch if your flight is delayed.

body.text: Can you fly direct from Antalya or İzmir to Cappadocia?

Yes—you can fly nonstop from both Antalya (AYT) and İzmir (ADB) to Kayseri (ASR), operated by [Pegasus Airlines](https://www.flypgs.com/en/cities/flights-to-kayseri) and SunExpress, with flight times around 1 hour 20 minutes ([FlightsFrom AYT–ASR](https://www.flightsfrom.com/AYT-ASR), [Skyscanner ADB–ASR](https://www.skyscanner.net/routes/adb/asr/izmir-to-kayseri.html)). Nevşehir (NAV) does not run regular direct coastal flights, making Kayseri the default airport for multi-region trips.

If your route links Ephesus (İzmir) or the Turquoise Coast (Antalya) with Cappadocia, booking ASR eliminates a four-hour layover in Istanbul. Just confirm seasonal frequency before locking hotel dates, as winter schedules trim coastal nonstops to select days of the week. Once your flights are set, map out your ground days with our [3-day Cappadocia itinerary](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/3-days-in-cappadocia) and [Göreme Open Air Museum timing guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/goreme-open-air-museum).

faq.q: Is there a public bus from Kayseri or Nevşehir airport to Göreme?
faq.a: No direct public bus runs from either terminal to Göreme, Uçhisar, or Ürgüp. Reaching Göreme by public transit requires taking a local bus or taxi into Kayseri or Nevşehir bus station first, then transferring to a regional minibus—slower and rarely cheaper than a €10–€15 shared shuttle.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a Cappadocia airport transfer?
faq.a: Book your transfer at least 48 to 72 hours before arrival, especially between April and October. Provide your exact flight number and hotel name so the operator tracks delays automatically.

faq.q: What if my flight to ASR or NAV is delayed?
faq.a: Reputable shared shuttles and private transfer companies monitor domestic flight numbers and hold vehicles for delayed arrivals. Shared shuttles for late-night international flights into Kayseri are less common, so book private transport if arriving on a European charter.

faq.q: Can I pick up a rental car at Nevşehir or Kayseri airport?
faq.a: Yes. Both airports have major rental desks, though Kayseri (ASR) stocks a much wider fleet of automatic vehicles and SUVs with longer desk hours than Nevşehir (NAV).

faq.q: Which airport is better if I have an early morning return flight?
faq.a: Nevşehir (NAV) saves 30 minutes of pre-dawn driving from Göreme or Uçhisar, letting you leave your hotel roughly 2 hours 15 minutes before departure instead of 2 hours 45 minutes for Kayseri (ASR).

faq.q: Do Cappadocia cave hotels arrange airport transfers?
faq.a: Almost all cave hotels book shared shuttles or private transfers for guests. Ask for the exact euro rate upfront—most hotels quote the standard local shuttle tariff (€10–€15 per person), while some add a small margin on private vans.
